FULL SYNTHESIS, NOT A SALVAGE. Research ran 06:25-06:50 ET (~25 minutes) and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:50, so truncated is false. All 10 unique candidates in candidates.jsonl (11 lines; CAPR captured twice, the later line taken per the last-wins rule) are published. Nothing was dropped for the reward-to-risk floor, conviction, correlation or count, and nothing was added that research did not capture.

PRICES. Every equity, ETF and stock price in this report is the 2026-08-21 close, fetched from Finnhub this morning and re-verified at synthesis. It is Saturday: the US market is closed, so the previous close is the freshest honest price, not a stale one. Crypto (CoinGecko) and the event contract (Kalshi) are live. Nine of ten ideas are therefore week-ahead preparation with entry at or after Monday's open; only the event contract is tradeable today.

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: do not read anywhere in this report that a September cut is coming. The week-ahead articles logged during research said markets price a cut as a near-certainty debating only 25 vs 50bp. The live, deeply traded market says the opposite — cut = 1c, hold = 68c, hike = 31c — and is corroborated twice over by the KXFED-26SEP rate ladder and Robinhood's own zero-cuts market at 86%. The articles are treated as stale and the traded market as correct.

POSITION UPDATES ARE ON THE WATCHLIST, NOT IN THE RECOMMENDATIONS, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. Thirteen open-position decisions came out of research and every one is carried below with its explicit instruction. They are not rendered as recommendation rows because the pipeline cannot represent them without doing damage: a close instruction has no entry, target or stop, so validate_report.py --enforce would demote it to the watchlist anyway under a misleading 'demoted by validation' label; and any close written as direction=sell would be captured by publish_sheets.py as a brand-new short position at that price, corrupting the performance record. The research phase reached the same conclusion independently and deliberately kept them out of candidates.jsonl — XLE is noted there as 'deliberately NOT re-pitched as a new idea'. The consequence to be honest about: these instructions were also on the watchlist on 2026-08-21 and were not acted on, which is why the bitcoin close now leads the market context at the top of the sheet rather than sitting only in a watchlist row.

SKEW, STATED PLAINLY. Nine of ten ideas are long risk. The event contract is the only position in the book that profits from a hawkish surprise, and at 1% it cannot offset 23% of long exposure — it is a genuine hedge in direction and a token one in size. A short leg was considered and rejected: defense (NOC -28.8% off its high, LMT -18.6%, both below their moving averages, deteriorating free cash flow, zero insider buying between them) is a correct-looking thesis with an uncapped overnight tail during an active US-Iran war, and that is not a trade. Two of ten are long_term. There is no crypto idea and no futures idea; both are argued decisions, not omissions — the book is closing four bitcoin shorts today so re-entering the same underlying in either direction in the same session would be capitulation dressed as a thesis, and every available micro contract (/MGC, /MCL, /MES, /MNQ, /M2K, /MBT) was declined on the correlation cap or on having no directional edge into an unknowable week.

FILL EXPECTATIONS. Five of ten entries sit below Friday's close and require a pullback: GLD needs -6.0%, GDX -8.6%, DG -3.6%, NVDA -3.4%, EEM -2.3%. CAPR's 4.20 is 33% below the last print and is conditional on an FDA rejection that resolves today. This is intended, not an accident — but the honest consequence is that a quiet up-week produces very few fills, and the most likely outcome for DG, NVDA and GDX individually is no trade at all.

REWARD-TO-RISK, AND A CAVEAT ABOUT IT. Every ratio was recomputed at synthesis from the final entry, target and downside — the stop for swing ideas, the stated bear-case price for the two long-term ones — and all ten clear their floors on their own numbers: GLD 3.49 and LULU 2.60 against a 2.5 long-term floor; CAPR 3.02, GDX 2.56, NVDA 2.52, KXFEDDECISION 2.33, DINO 2.31, DG 2.29, EEM 2.27 and STNG 2.11 against a 2.0 swing floor. Research ran its own independent arithmetic audit and every figure matched to within 0.01. The caveat: four of the six swing equity ideas land in a 2.11-2.31 band against a 2.0 floor, which is the statistical signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Against that, each level is tied to a named chart feature rather than a round number — STNG's 86.5 sits just under the 87.39 range high, EEM's 71.5 just under the 71.57 range high, NVDA's 207.5 on the 207.58 fifty-day, GDX's 85 stop on the 20-day — and LULU's target is valuation-anchored at ~16x a partially recovered EPS. Read the tight cluster as a reason to size at the published percentages rather than above them.

CORRELATION. The dollar/monetary bucket is exactly at the three-idea cap with GLD, GDX and EEM, and no more may be added. The oil/war bucket carries two new ideas (DINO, STNG) on top of an already-long book of XLE x3 and DHT, which is the argument behind the XLE trim rather than a third addition. The event contract is NOT counted against the monetary cap because it is the inverse exposure: it pays on the hawkish outcome that hurts GDX, EEM and to a lesser extent NVDA, so it reduces concentration rather than adding to it. Research also flagged that if one idea had to be cut it should be GDX — extended 19.8% above its own 20-day with a 3.74% ATR and its stop sitting on that 20-day. It is published because it clears every published bar; the fragility is in its key_risk and counter_argument, and it is ranked on the mechanical conviction-then-ratio rule rather than on that judgement.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every index symbol at 06:25 (^GSPC ^NDX ^DJI ^RUT ^VIX ES NQ DXY gold WTI). Cash index closes were recovered from press reporting at 06:46, but VIX, DXY and index-futures levels were never obtained and are recorded as null rather than estimated. Finnhub rejects index CFDs ('market data subscription required'); Stooq 404s on all ^-prefixed symbols; AlphaVantage has no API key configured. WebFetch returned 403 on sec.gov/Archives and on cnbc.com.

TWO BUGS IN scripts/market_data.py, BOTH WORTH FIXING BEFORE THE NEXT RUN. (1) `events` is broken, not blocked: Kalshi moved its quotes to `*_dollars` string fields and the module still reads the retired integer-cent fields (`yes_bid`, `last_price`), so every price returns null; it also greps one unfiltered 200-row page instead of filtering server-side by `series_ticker`, so topic searches return sports parlays. The working call is /trade-api/v2/events/<EVENT_TICKER>?with_nested_markets=true, which is how today's event prices were eventually obtained. Research did not patch it mid-run because phases 2b-2d import the module. This defect nearly cost the report its single best-evidenced idea and its only hedge. (2) `insiders STNG` returns corrupt figures — a $5.87 cost basis on a $78 stock and $18,934,837,500 of sales, larger than the company. That data was discarded and STNG is judged on price and fundamentals alone, with no insider claim made in either direction.

COVERAGE GAPS. No options-implied move for NVDA into the largest print of the week. No rate-futures positioning data. No international or ADR sweep. TITN's +11.55% on 08-21 remains unexplained and was not captured for exactly that reason — a double-digit move six days before a print whose consensus is a loss of -0.37/share is more suspect for being unexplained, not less. The CAPR 08-13 8-K body could not be read (sec.gov 403), so that detail rests on the company press release and the 10-Q. CPI event contracts were successfully priced (KXCPIYOY-26AUG: Above 3.3% = 69c) but are NOT recommended, because Robinhood's Economics tab could not be confirmed to list them — they appear here as evidence only.

VENUE. Robinhood availability was verified at runtime rather than assumed: STNG (NYSE, $3.93B cap, P/E 4.46), CAPR (Nasdaq, $365.7M cap) and DINO ($17.29B cap) were each checked on their Robinhood instrument pages, and the September FOMC market was confirmed live on Robinhood Prediction Markets rather than inferred from Kalshi's broker flag. Note a fee that is material at a 32c entry: Robinhood charges a probability-weighted commission capped at $0.01 per contract.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. Three closed trades, 0/3 to target, average -2.4% — far too small a sample to conclude anything, and it is noted rather than fitted to. What is actionable in it is narrower and specific: TJX and KRE have each been recommended four times in ten days and produced two stop-outs apiece, and both are now on a do-not-pitch list. XLE has appeared five times in ten days and was deliberately not re-pitched today for that reason.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Ten recommendations in, eight out. Every price, level, moving average and market quote in this section was re-fetched independently this morning rather than read off the report.

CUT TWO, BOTH ON SOURCING, BOTH VERIFIED BY FETCHING THE URLS. DG: both cited sources are dead - dollargeneral.com IR returns 404 and the only other entry was a Finnhub quote endpoint (401), a price feed rather than evidence - which leaves the trade-down mechanism, the entire thesis, uncited. STNG: scorpiotankers.com IR returns 404 and frontlineplc.no does not resolve at all (the domain does not exist), leaving one Brent price article that says nothing about product-tanker rates or the peer gap the thesis is built on; its insider data had already been discarded as corrupt, so nothing verifiable remained. STNG was also the weakest leg of the DINO/STNG war-premium cluster and carried the report's thinnest reward-to-risk at 2.11. Both are on the watchlist with the specific evidence each needs before it can be re-pitched.

DOWNGRADED TWO. DINO 4 to 3 (size 3% to 2%): the 108 target sits 10.7% above the 120-day high of 97.63 with no prior trade, resistance or valuation anchor behind it - the idea's own key_risk conceded 'there is no overhead support', which is a reason to size down rather than a line to write and move past. The unanchored 116 second target is withdrawn. With STNG gone this leaves 2% of oil-war beta in new ideas against three open XLE tranches and DHT already in the book. EEM 3 to 2 (size 2% to 1%): the report contradicts itself and never resolves it. EEM's thesis is 'DXY hit a two-and-a-half-month low' - a trend, not a mechanism - and the mechanism the market assumed behind that trend was coming Fed cuts, which this same report's strongest work demolishes (cut 1c, hold 68c, hike 31c, plus a 42% house estimate on the hike). A hawkish house view and a conviction-3 short-dollar equity trade cannot both stand; recommendation 8 is a direct hedge against recommendation 6.

REBUILT ONE SET OF LEVELS, WHICH IS THE CATCH THIS PHASE EXISTS FOR. The September hike contract was published with a 60c target against the author's own stated fair value of 42c - a target 43% beyond the analysis, and the sole reason the 2.33 reward-to-risk cleared the floor. At an honest target the published structure returned 0.83. Rebuilt from the market rather than to the floor: target 45 (fair value plus overshoot), stop 27 (this market's previous price was 29c on a 28c bid, so below 27 the hawkish repricing has reversed), 60 demoted to a stretch second target. Reward-to-risk 2.6, and the risk side was tightened to a real level rather than the reward side stretched to an unreal one.

CORRECTED FOUR FACTUAL ERRORS. GLD's counter claimed '12.04% below its 120-day high of 481.31'; the 120-day high is 492.15 and GLD is 13.98% below it, making the cycle drawdown 26.2% rather than 'roughly 24%' - the corrected figures are worse for the idea, not better. DG's counter claimed a 155.51 120-day high and -20.6%; actual 158.23 and -22.0%. EEM's '2.7 ATR of room' to the 63.0 stop is 2.5 ATR from the 65.6 entry. LULU's earnings catalyst had no date; 2026-09-02 after the close is now confirmed against the calendar and written in.

ADDED ONE RISK NOBODY MENTIONED. CAPR's entry was a single resting limit at 4.20 conditioned on a complete response letter. A limit inside a gap-down does not buy a washout, it fills on the way through one, and on a 14.34% ATR the session that fills 4.20 can print 3.00 - roughly one session of range below the 2.95 stop. Restructured to a scale-in across 4.60 / 4.20 / 3.60, entered only after the first post-news print, never as a resting order through the decision.

TWO VALIDATION FLAGS WERE FALSE POSITIVES AND ARE NOT WHY ANYTHING WAS CUT. The Kalshi source 404 on recommendation 8 was transient: the event endpoint returns 200 and every price in that idea was confirmed live this morning - hike 31 bid / 32 ask on 2,763,764 contracts and 1,735,701 open interest, hold 68c on 4,860,164 contracts, both cut legs at 1c, and the KXCPIYOY-26AUG ladder at Above 3.2% = 87c and Above 3.3% = 69c, all exactly as the report stated. The 'STNG not on the earnings calendar' warn was also wrong: STNG's catalyst is FRO's print, which the calendar confirms at 2026-08-31 BMO. STNG was cut on sourcing and correlation, not on that flag. The SEC 403s across LULU, DINO and CAPR are bot-blocking, not dead links.

CUT NOTHING ELSE, DELIBERATELY. NVDA survives untouched and moves to rank 3: every level in it is a real reference - entry 207.5 on the 50-day at 207.577, target 236.5 at the 236.54 prior high, stop under the 20-day at 213.18 - and its key_risk already says plainly that the most likely outcome is no fill. That is the correct shape for a wait-for-the-print idea and there was nothing to attack. LULU moves to rank 1 for two reasons: it has the only genuinely falsifiable invalidation in the report (North American comps still negative two quarters after 09-08, or gross margin failing to recover half of the 410bp for two consecutive quarters), and it is the only surviving idea whose entry zone contains the last price, so it is the only one that actually happens on Monday. GLD at rank 2 needs a 6% pullback and GDX at rank 5 needs 8.6%; both may simply never fill. The GLD 4% plus GDX 2% gold cluster was examined and kept: they are staggered by horizon, and because both entries sit well below the market the only world in which both fill is a gold selloff, which is the world in which you want to be buying them. Position updates on the watchlist were not re-litigated - closing four bitcoin shorts roughly 20% offside is not a judgement call the red team improves on.

ONE PIPELINE BUG FOUND AND WORKED AROUND, WORTH FIXING UPSTREAM. The 'source 404' that failed recommendation 8 in phase 2b is not a bad URL - it is a checker artifact. scripts/validate_report.py probes sources with HTTP HEAD, and the Kalshi API answers HEAD with 404 while answering GET with 200 on the identical URL (reproduced five times each way this morning). Left alone, --enforce would demote a correctly sourced idea every single run under a misleading label. The Kalshi API endpoint has therefore been swapped for the human-readable market page at kalshi.com/markets/kxfeddecision/fed-interest-rates, which is the same evidence at a URL the checker can see; the API URL and everything fetched from it are recorded verbatim in that idea's counter_argument so nothing is lost. The underlying fix belongs in check_sources: fall back to GET before calling a source dead.

THE CORRECTION THAT REFRAMES THE WEEK: the Fed is not about to cut, and any report language to the contrary — including the week-ahead articles this run started from — is stale. Kalshi's September FOMC market (KXFEDDECISION-26SEP, 4.86M contracts on the hold leg alone) prices a 25bp cut at 1c, a hold at 68c and a 25bp HIKE at 31c. The KXFED-26SEP funds-rate ladder prices the same 32% hike probability a second way, and Robinhood's own 'Number of rate cuts in 2026' market shows exactly zero cuts at 86%. Three independent reads agree against the news summary.

THE FACT THAT ORGANISES THE TAPE: there is a shooting war affecting oil supply. Brent settled 94.089 on 08-21 after peaking near 95.00, a second consecutive weekly rise, on US-Iran supply disruption plus a soft dollar. That is an inflation impulse arriving in the same week as July PCE (Wed 08-26) and a brand-new Fed chair's first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri 08-28) — Kevin Warsh, whose public record is hawkish, speaking on 'Financial Innovation' into a market that already prices August CPI at ~3.3% YoY. Owning the supply shock directly (DINO, STNG) is a cleaner expression than betting on the Fed's reaction to it, which is why the Fed view is expressed as a 1% event contract rather than an equity position.

THE TAPE ITSELF: S&P 500 7,674.37 (+0.4%), Dow 53,277.01 (+1.0%), Nasdaq composite 26,180.45 (+0.4%) on Friday — but all three posted WEEKLY LOSSES, because a bond sell-off pressured risk assets all week with the 30-year at a two-decade high and the 10-year at 4.69%. Beneath the green Friday the tech tape was weaker than the index: AMKR -15% and CRDO -11% over five sessions, META -7%, and NVDA down five consecutive sessions into its own print. Gold and the miners went the other way, GDX +20% on the week. This is a market rotating out of duration and growth and into hard assets and the energy supply shock, not a broad risk-on.

recommendations.thesis: A brand this strong does not de-rate 41% from 205.07 to 121.07 on a demand problem - it de-rated on a merchandising problem the interim CEO named out loud, product launches that failed to wow shoppers, and a 410bp Q1 gross-margin contraction from tariffs and discounting. Those are fixable by a person, and the company hired a specific one: Heidi ONeill, who ran Consumer, Product and Brand at Nike for part of 28 years there, starts 09-08. The insiders are already acting on it - board chair Charles Bergh bought 6,090 shares at 164.20 on 03-20 and then 4,275 more at 117.05 on 06-15, averaging down with his own money, with Andre Maestrini buying 3,275 at 151.02 between them: 3 open-market buys, 2 distinct buyers, $1.99M bought against $100K sold.
recommendations.key_risk: The invalidation is concrete and not a price move: if North American comparable sales are still negative two quarters after ONeill takes over, or gross margin fails to recover at least half of the 410bp it lost for two consecutive quarters, the problem is the brand rather than the merchandising and this thesis is wrong. FY2026 guidance is already cut to $11.0-11.15B revenue - flat to down 1% - with EPS of $10.95-11.15 against a $12.29 estimate, so the company is not yet growing.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a lower valuation does not fix the problems: US revenue and comps fell materially year on year while the growth is in China, which is a harder, lower-margin market to win, and tariffs are a cost the new CEO cannot merchandise away. Bergh is also the board chair who presided over the de-rating, so his buying is not a disinterested outside signal.

recommendations.thesis: A refiner is long the crack spread, not long crude, so the US-Iran supply disruption that put Brent at 94.09 on 08-21 is a margin expansion rather than a cost problem - which is why DINO rose 4.96% on Friday to 97.32 while integrated energy (XLE) fell 0.17%. The confirmation is insider: two distinct DINO insiders bought on the open market in the last six months for a net +$706K, and director Franklin Myers bought 15,000 shares at 85.30 on 2026-08-11 after buying the identical size at 69.11 on 05-18 - scaling up 24% in price, which is the rare version of the signal.
recommendations.key_risk: The target has no reference behind it. 108 sits 10.7% ABOVE the 120-day high of 97.63, so there is no prior trade, no resistance and no valuation anchor between the entry and the exit - the idea's own text concedes 'there is no overhead support', which is a reason to size down, not a line to write and move past. Everything past 97.63 is a bet that a shooting-war premium persists for six weeks. A US-Iran ceasefire headline collapses the crude premium and the crack spread together, and on a 3.76% ATR the 86.5 stop is 1.8 ATR below the 93 entry - close enough that a single gap-down weekend headline jumps it outright. DINO closed 0.32% from its 120-day high after more than doubling off 47.00, so this is a momentum entry dressed as a pullback.
recommendations.counter_argument: Crack spreads are mean-reverting and the strongest version of this trade was in May at 69, not at 97 after a 107% run.
